newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish banks see 1996 inflation at 19.9 pct - poll.
newsitem.headline: Polish banks see 1996 inflation at 19.9 pct - poll.

text.p: Polish banks have raised their 1996 consumer price growth forecast by 0.6 percentage point to 19.9 percent in September, a survey of 208 institutions conducted by the private polling institute Pentor showed.
A Reuter poll of Poland's 26 largest banks earlier this month showed they expected year-on-year inflation to fall to 18.6 percent in December from 20.5 percent in August.
The government's 1996 price growth target is 17 percent.
Pentor said on Tuesday that banks expected the Polish zloty to fall to about 2.81 to the dollar by the end of the year from Monday's fixing at 2.7855 per dollar.
The Reuter poll showed the zloty easing to 2.85 against the dollar by December 31, 1996.
